# Rust golden capture (U-DSP.1)

Generated by `backend/internal/dsp/testdata/capture/main.go` — do not edit by hand.
Re-capture with `cd backend && go run ./internal/dsp/testdata/capture/main.go`;
the same command with `-check` re-runs the capture and exits non-zero on any drift.

Prerequisites for both modes: a built reference engine
(`cd sync-engine && cargo build --release`), `cargo` with the harness's crates in
the local registry cache (the emitter builds offline), `ffmpeg`, and `testfiles/`
(Tier B needs the four real fixtures). Tier A needs no media. The synthetic tier is
produced by the Rust harness's own generator: the tool copies `sync-engine/` into a
scratch directory, drops the sibling `capture/emit.rs` in as `tests/emit.rs` and runs
`cargo test --test emit`, so `tests/common/mod.rs` is compiled, not re-implemented.

Every number below is the reference engine's own output (`SyncResult` rounded to
three decimals by `job.rs:121-123`), copied verbatim from the golden JSON.
**margin to 0.10** is `correlation_quality - 0.10`, the distance to
`analyze.LowQualityThreshold`; a checkpoint marked **thin** sits below 0.15
(plan conflict (e): the margin is for the maintainer's sign-off, not the coder's).

## Tier B — real material (committed excerpts)

Each row is one checkpoint of `analyze.DefaultCheckpointPositionsPct`
(10/25/40/55/70/85 %), cut from the production decode of the fixture pair at
`analyze.sliceWindow`'s position. The excerpt **is** the analysed window, so the
recorded payload asks for `slice_start_sec = 0`; the source position it was cut
from is the `source_start_sec` field of each golden row.

Minions is the cross-language pair: there is no shared reference language, so the
band is the 30-200 Hz low-pass and the peaks are weak. Some of its offsets are
spurious peaks rather than a real alignment; they are recorded exactly as the
reference engine measured them, and the 40 % row is **thin**.

## Excerpt length and the committed-size budget

The plan asks for 30 s excerpts and `<= 8 MB` of committed testdata with each WAV
`<= 640 KB`. Those do not fit together. A 30 s 8 kHz mono file is 480,044 B at
16-bit and 960,044 B at 32-bit float; the 24 Tier B excerpts alone would weigh
11.5 MB (16-bit) or 23 MB (float) before a single synthetic file is committed.
The committed set therefore uses:

- Tier B: 10 s excerpts, 8 kHz mono 16-bit — 24 files, 160,044 B each,
  ~3.67 MiB total.
- Tier A: the generator's own samples, truncated to the region the harness
  analyses (`[0, 15 s)` = 240,044 B per 16-bit mono file); the stereo case,
  which the harness writes as 32-bit float stereo, is committed as 16-bit
  stereo (480,044 B for the same 15 s) because a float copy of the analysed
  region is 960,068 B and breaks the 640 KB per-file cap. The quantisation is
  the harness's own rounding rule (`round(clamp(s,-1,1) * 32767)`).

Every committed file is therefore 16-bit PCM (`U-DSP.3`'s `/32768` divisor); the
32-bit float decode path is covered by that unit's own table tests, not here.

The truncation cannot move a number: the payload still asks for
`slice_start_sec = 5` for Tier A, and the engine reads only frames
`[40000, 120000)`, which are byte-identical to the full-length file.
Tier B is re-encoded to 16-bit by ffmpeg because 32-bit float excerpts do not
fit the per-file cap at any useful length; the production decode that feeds
them is still `pcm_f32le` and the band filter is verbatim, and the golden
describes the committed 16-bit bytes (that is also what exercises U-DSP.3's
`/32768` divisor). The consequences are recorded rather than hidden: excerpt
numbers are not the production 190 s checkpoint numbers (they never were), and
the quality values above are the ones the Go port must reproduce on these files.
The capture tool prints the measured committed total on every run.

## Reading the table

- `offset_ms = t_target - t_donor` (`main.rs`), so a positive value means the
  target's audio runs late relative to the donor.
- Tier A cases carry the Rust suite's own bounds in the case label
  (`expect … ±… ms, q >= …`, from `tests/golden.rs`).
- Tier B has no expected offset: the excerpt value *is* the expectation.
- **thin**: `quality < 0.15`. U-DSP.9 asserts `quality_go >= 0.12` and
  `|Δquality| <= 0.02` per checkpoint; a thin or sub-0.12 Rust value makes that
  assertion unmeetable and is a sign-off matter, not something to round away.
